newsitem.title: USA: Convicted Fla. killer "Crazy Joe" gets new trial.
newsitem.headline: Convicted Fla. killer "Crazy Joe" gets new trial.

text.p: The Florida Supreme Court Thursday approved a new trial for Joseph "Crazy Joe" Spaziano, a motorcycle gang chieftain who spent two decades on death row before the key witness against him recanted.

In a unanimous ruling, the state Supreme Court upheld a decision by a lower court judge last year that the recanted testimony from witness Tony Dilisio was significant enough to "probably produce a new result upon retrial."

Spaziano, the leader of the Outlaws motorcycle gang when it built a drug and prostitution network in central Florida in the early 1970s, was sentenced to die for the 1973 murder of Laura Lynn Harberts, an 18-year-old hospital clerk from Orlando.

At trial, Delisio told the jury that Spaziano had taken him to a rural dump and shown him the decomposing remains of two women. He painted a gruesome picture of how Harberts was raped and mutilated by Spaziano.

Authorities at the time used hypnosis to help him recall the incident. The state high court has since banned hypnotically induced testimony as unreliable, but the prohibition came after the Spaziano trial.
In a 1995 story, the Miami Herald reported that Dilisio had recanted the testimony, saying he invented the story to satisfy police investigators.

Last year, the Supreme Court ordered a new hearing in the case, citing Delisio's statements that he had lied during the trial. After hearing from 26 witnesses, state Circuit Judge O.H. Eaton ruled that Dilisio may well have made up testimony critical to the state's case.
The death sentence was vacated and a new trial ordered. The state appealed.
"It is clear to us that there is evidence in this record to support the trial court's decision," the state Supreme Court wrote Thursday in an unsigned opinion.
Spaziano survived five death warrants. In 1995, Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles halted his execution less than two weeks before he was to be put to death in Florida's electric chair.
